stories.title: Gradual restoration of excise 'more manageable' - Harris
stories.summary: Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris has said the extension of excise reductions on petrol and diesel to 1 September will bring clarity and provide help to "hard-pressed" people and businesses. The current measures, which were due to expire at the end of July, have resulted in an excise duty cut of 27 cent on a litre of petrol and 32 cent on a litre of diesel, when VAT is included. The extension of the reductions, which are expected to cost €270 million, is due to be considered by Cabinet today. Speaking on his way into Cabinet, Mr Harris said: "I'm very conscious of the fact that petrol and diesel prices are, thankfully, falling.

stories.title: New draft guidelines for rural and Gaeltacht housing due
stories.summary: New draft planning guidelines for rural and Gaeltacht housing are to be published. Minister for Housing James Browne and Minister of State John Cummins will bring proposals to the Cabinet this morning which will ease some planning restrictions. The aim of this draft National Planning Statement is to provide more consistency around rural housing. It is seeking to allow new rural homes to be built, along with preventing urban sprawl, as well as regenerating rural towns and villages.

stories.title: Teenage boy dies following fall from e-scooter in Carlow
stories.summary: A teenage boy has died after he fell from an e-scooter in Carlow last night. The boy, who was aged in his late teens, was travelling on the e-scooter with another person when they fell on Carpenters Way in Carlow town at around 8.30pm. He was taken to St Luke's Hospital in Kilkenny with serious injuries, before being transferred to Beaumont Hospital in Dublin, where he later died. The second person, an adult aged in his late teens, was assessed at the scene, but did not require hospital treatment.

stories.title: What you need to know about new customs charges

The EU-wide €3 per item fee is designed to ensure fair competition and protect consumers from imports that don't meet EU standards. But how will what is probably the most significant customs change for Irish consumers since the UK left the single market work? From 1 July, all purchases entering Ireland from outside the European Union will be subject to new customs charges.

stories.title: Tributes paid to Mullingar locals killed in Spanish crash
stories.summary: Tributes have been paid to the three people from Co Westmeath killed in a car crash in Spain. Mark McCullagh, his partner Michaela Newcombe, and his sister-in-law Amy McCullagh were killed in the crash, which occurred near Malaga at around 2.30am on Sunday morning. A fourth Irish person was seriously injured in the two-vehicle collision. The man, who is also from Mullingar, was taken to hospital for treatment.

stories.title: Key Venezuela seaport reopens following earthquakes
stories.summary: The United States military has repaired and reopened a key seaport in the hardest hit area of Venezuela, as the country began burying more than 1,700 victims of twin earthquakes that have left tens of thousands still missing. Five days after powerful back-to-back quakes flattened entire neighbourhoods, the task of recovering bodies loomed large while hopes of finding survivors faded. By the latest official count, some 1,700 people are dead and 5,000 are injured, with no governmental word on the number missing. Other estimates place these in the tens of thousands. The Port of La Guaira re-opened, where an AFP correspondent observed a warehouse storing hundreds of unidentified bodies encased in white and black body bags as well as a few coffins. The USS Fort Lauderdale was docked and delivering aid.
